proposals.before: Wang Gong of Shaanzhou fought his brother Ke for Hezhong; he sent Sizhao to aid Ke, beat Gong at Yishi, and took three of his generals.
proposals.after: Wang Gong of Shaanzhou contended with his elder brother Ke for Hezhong; [Jin] sent Sizhao to aid Ke, who defeated Gong at Yishi and captured three of his generals.
proposals.reason: Chinese 遣嗣昭助珂 has a silent subject from the Jin/Taizu narrative, not Wang Gong; 其兄 marks Ke as the elder brother.

proposals.before: Wang Gong of Shaan Prefecture contended with his elder brother Ke for rule in Hezhong; he sent Sizhao to aid Ke and defeated Gong at Yishi, capturing three of his generals.
proposals.after: Wang Gong of Shaan Prefecture contended with his elder brother Ke for rule in Hezhong; [Jin] sent Sizhao to aid Ke, who defeated Gong at Yishi, capturing three of his generals.
proposals.reason: The silent subject of 遣嗣昭 is Taizu/Jin, not Wang Gong; making Gong the sender reverses the campaign.

proposals.before: Hearing Taizu had come himself, Sizhao abandoned the city and fled straight into the ambush and was crushed.
proposals.after: Hearing Liang Taizu had come himself, Sizhao abandoned the city and fled straight into the ambush and was crushed.
proposals.reason: Chinese 梁太祖 is Liang Taizu; dropping Liang conflates him with Jin Taizu in the same chapter.

proposals.before: At Willow Hu Jin lost; Zhou Dewei fell.
proposals.after: At Huliu, Jin lost; Zhou Dewei fell.
proposals.reason: 胡柳 is the place Huliu (Huliu Slope), not a calque 'Willow Hu'; the current rendering obscures the battle name.

proposals.before: Taizu panicked and planned escape to Yunzhou; Cunxin urged flight to the Khitan; Sizhao and Consort Liu protested until he stayed.
proposals.after: Taizu panicked and planned escape to Yunzhou; Cunxin and others urged flight to the Khitan; Sizhao protested that it was impossible, and Consort Liu said the same, so he stopped.
proposals.reason: Chinese 李存信等 includes companions, and 嗣昭力爭 / 劉太妃亦言之 are separate speeches, not a fused joint protest.

proposals.before: Of Sizhao's seven sons, under Mingzong Jineng was killed for flogging his mother's stewardess to death; her kin cried rebellion, and he and Jixi died—only Jizhong survived.
proposals.after: Of Sizhao's seven sons, under Mingzong Jieneng was condemned for flogging to death a storehouse maid of his mother's; the maid's household reported a rising, and he and Jixi were both killed—only Jizhong escaped.
proposals.reason: 繼能 is Jieneng/Jineng; 主藏婢 is a storehouse maid, and 婢家告變 is her household's accusation, not a vague 'kin cried rebellion' only.
太尉 is Grand Commandant (or Defender-in-chief), not Grand Preceptor (太師/太傅).

proposals.before: Jin had hammered Zhao’s Changshan for years; Cunxiao usually led the van and seized Lincheng and Yuan Clan.
proposals.after: Jin had hammered Zhao’s Changshan for years; Cunxiao usually led the van and seized Lincheng and Yuanshi.
proposals.reason: 元氏 is the county Yuanshi, not a calque 'Yuan Clan'.
太尉 is Grand Commandant (Defender-in-chief), not Grand Preceptor (太師/太傅).

proposals.before: Li Cunxian came from Xuzhou; born Wang Xian.
proposals.after: Li Cunxian came from Xu Prefecture (Xuzhou 許州); born Wang Xian.
proposals.reason: 許州 is Xu Prefecture in Henan, not 徐州 (the usual 'Xuzhou').

decisions.after: Wang Gong of Shaanzhou contended with his elder brother Ke for control of Hezhong. Taizu sent Sizhao to aid Ke; Sizhao defeated Gong at Yishi and captured three of his generals.
decisions.reason: Taizu is the omitted subject of 遣, while Sizhao remains the subject of 敗 and 獲. The proposal correctly removes Gong as sender but wrongly makes Ke the victor.

decisions.after: Of Sizhao’s seven sons, under Mingzong his son Jineng was condemned for flogging to death a maid in charge of his mother’s storehouse. The maid’s family accused Jineng of rebellion; he and his younger brother Jixi were both executed, and only Jizhong narrowly escaped.
decisions.reason: 繼能 is Jineng, not Jieneng. 主藏婢 is a maid responsible for the mother’s storehouse, 婢家 is the maid’s family, and the final clause says Jizhong narrowly escaped.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 嗣昭七子，至明宗時，子繼能坐笞殺其母主藏婢，婢家告變，言繼能反，與其弟繼襲皆見殺，惟一子繼忠僅免。
